title: Maximum Twin Sum of a Linked List
description:
In a singly linked list of **even** length `n`, the `i`-th node (0-indexed) and the `(n - 1 - i)`-th node are called **twins** for every `0 <= i < n / 2`. The **twin sum** of a twin pair is the sum of the two nodes' values.

Given the `head` of an even-length singly linked list, return the maximum twin sum across all pairs. Aim for `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes n is even and lies in the range [2, 10^4].
hints: Use slow and fast pointers to find the start of the second half of the list.
Reverse the second half in-place, then walk the first half and reversed second half in lockstep while tracking the maximum sum `first.val + second.val`.

examples.explanation: Twin pairs are (5, 1) with sum 6 and (4, 2) with sum 6, so the maximum is 6.
Twin pairs are (4, 3) with sum 7 and (2, 2) with sum 4, so the maximum is 7.
The only twin pair is (1, 100000) with sum 100001.
